cards.title: Endpoint Independence from Terminal Slope Estimation
cards.claim: Parameters such as Cmax, Tmax, AUClast, and AUMClast do not require Lambda Z estimation and remain reportable when terminal slope estimation fails. Conversely, parameters like AUCinf, Vz, CL, and MRTinf depend on Lambda Z; if Lambda Z is not estimable (e.g., due to insufficient points or non-negative slope), these parameters are omitted or flagged. CLss is a distinct estimand for steady-state data and does not rely on single-dose terminal slope.
conditions: Applicable when terminal phase data is insufficient for regression (e.g., <3 points for non-bolus, <2 for bolus) or slope is not negative.
Software automatically omits Lambda Z-dependent parameters and issues a warning.
required_inputs: Concentration-time data with clear Cmax and Tlast.
Dosing information (bolus vs. infusion) to determine point count requirements for Lambda Z.
limitations: AUClast is truncated at Tlast; it does not represent total exposure if elimination is incomplete.
Software defaults for point counts (e.g., 3 points) are algorithmic constraints, not universal scientific validity criteria.
cards.downstream_use: Report observed exposure metrics (AUClast, Cmax) for PK/PD analysis when terminal phase is undefined. Do not impute or extrapolate CL/Vz without valid Lambda Z.
cards.retrieval_keywords: NCA endpoints with unreliable terminal slope and sparse destructive sampling

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
